articles.title: ACR Appropriateness Criteria® Chronic Liver Disease: 2026 Update.
articles.abstract: Chronic liver disease, caused by a range of etiologies, can lead to progressive liver function deterioration, hepatic fibrosis, cirrhosis, and, ultimately, end-stage liver disease. With cirrhosis and end-stage liver disease, complications include portal hypertension, gastrointestinal hemorrhage, refractory ascites, hepatic encephalopathy, and primary hepatocellular carcinoma. Imaging plays an important role in the diagnosis, treatment response assessment, and surveillance of chronic liver disease, specifically of hepatic hemochromatosis, steatosis, and fibrosis, in an effort to prevent progression to cirrhosis. This document reviews the imaging modalities best suited for these clinical scenarios, and a summary of current evidence is provided to support the use of various modalities for each of the clinical contexts. The American College of Radiology Appropriateness Criteria are evidence-based guidelines for specific clinical conditions that are reviewed annually by a multidisciplinary expert panel. The guideline development and revision include an extensive analysis of current medical literature from peer reviewed journals and the application of well-established methodologies (RAND/UCLA Appropriateness Method and Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation or GRADE) to rate the appropriateness of imaging and treatment procedures for specific clinical scenarios. In those instances where evidence is lacking or equivocal, expert opinion may supplement the available evidence to recommend imaging or treatment.

articles.title: 3D and 4D Hysterosalpingo-Contrast Sonography: Advanced Tubal Patency Assessment.
articles.abstract: Female infertility affects approximately 15% of couples of reproductive age, with tubal disease responsible for up to one-third of cases. Therefore, accurate, minimally invasive evaluation of tubal patency is a cornerstone of fertility assessment. Among the available modalities, including hysterosalpingography (HSG), MR HSG, and laparoscopic chromopertubation, hysterosalpingo-contrast sonography (HyCoSy) has gained prominence as a valuable alternative to conventional methods due to its safety, accessibility, and diagnostic reliability. Recent advances in contrast-enhanced US involving the use of second-generation microbubble agents combined with three-dimensional (3D) and four-dimensional (4D) acquisition technologies have significantly improved the performance of HyCoSy. These developments enable real-time volumetric visualization of the uterine cavity and fallopian tubes, enhancing both anatomic delineation and functional assessment of tubal patency. In addition, combined 3D and 4D (3D-4D) HyCoSy enables complementary evaluation of uterine morphology, adnexal structures, and associated infertility-related disorders such as endometriosis and adhesions, facilitating a comprehensive "one-stop" reproductive imaging approach. This article is intended to serve as a practical guide to performing 3D-4D HyCoSy with microbubble contrast agents, including preparation, technical parameters, and findings interpretation. In addition, the authors compare HyCoSy with conventional techniques, review characteristic imaging patterns of tubal patency and occlusion, and discuss potential pitfalls and preventive strategies. As an advanced US technology combined with a dynamic functional perspective, 3D-4D HyCoSy represents a powerful, cost-effective, and patient-friendly tool for integrated fertility evaluation in modern radiology practices.

articles.title: Personalized 90Y Dosimetry: A Practical Framework for Intent-based Radioembolization.
articles.abstract: Yttrium 90 transarterial radioembolization has evolved from a palliative lobar therapy for advanced liver malignancies into a versatile potentially curative treatment across hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) stages, intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (iCCA), and liver metastases. Central to this evolution is the shift from empirical population-based activity prescriptions to personalized dosimetry, tailoring administered activity to each patient's anatomy, tumor biology, treatment intent, and microsphere distribution to optimize tumor absorbed dose while constraining normal tissue exposure. Prospective studies have demonstrated that personalized dosimetry significantly improves tumor response and overall survival compared with conventional dosing. Despite this evidence, clinical adoption remains inconsistent. In this review, the authors aim to address that gap by providing a practical intent-based framework for implementation. They present dosimetric principles, activity prescription methods, and dose-response evidence across HCC, iCCA, and liver metastases, with practical recommendations organized by treatment intent. Treatment intent, whether curative or palliative, is the primary determinant of dosimetric strategy, guiding selection of the dosimetry model, target dose, and normal liver dose constraints. The authors review pretreatment planning work flows and posttreatment verification and present a practical decision algorithm integrating clinical intent, imaging, and dosimetry modeling. ©RSNA, 2026 See the invited commentary by Malone and Toskich in this issue.

An International Study of Factors Affecting Variability of Dosimetry Calculations, Part 6: Lessons Learned, Achievable Variability, and the Road Ahead.
articles.abstract: Personalized radiopharmaceutical therapies rely on accurate and reproducible absorbed dose estimates. However, substantial variability persists because of differences in imaging protocols, segmentation, time-activity curve fitting and integration, and dose calculation implementation. The Society of Nuclear Medicine and Molecular Imaging 177Lu Dosimetry Challenge was a 5-task international study designed to isolate sources of variability in image-based dosimetry workflows. In this final publication, we integrate findings across the series and perform a retrospective analysis of the original full-workflow submissions to estimate the reduction in variability achievable through methodologic consistency and quality assurance. Methods: In this final analysis, the original task 1 end-to-end SPECT/CT workflow submissions were reevaluated to generate a refined task 1 dataset by excluding previously identified processing or reporting mistakes, as well as submissions with methodologic choices inconsistent with the recommendations derived from the challenge. Exclusion criteria included nonstandard volume-of-interest (VOI) definitions, inconsistent VOI handling, inappropriate time-activity curve fitting and integration, and omission of required mass scaling. Variability was quantified using the interquartile range and quartile coefficient of dispersion (QCD). Results: The refined task 1 analysis showed that a substantial fraction of the observed variability is potentially avoidable. Exclusions reduced the analyzed dataset by approximately 50% and narrowed absorbed dose distributions for most organs and lesions. For patient A, QCD decreased for total kidney (23.1% to 3.0%), spleen (24.2% to 7.8%), and lesion 1 (22.8% to 13.3%). For patient B, organ variability also decreased (12.6% to 8.2% in the liver and 15.3% to 10.9% in the left kidney), although variability for some lesions decreased less substantially. Findings across the challenge indicated that, among the workflow steps evaluated, segmentation and time-activity curve fitting/integration were the dominant contributors to variability, whereas variability from the absorbed dose calculation step alone was generally small once upstream inputs were standardized. Conclusion: A substantial portion of variability in radiopharmaceutical therapy dosimetry is potentially avoidable through standardization and quality assurance. Under more standardized conditions, organ absorbed dose estimates showed markedly lower variability, with QCD values as low as 3%. These results support implementation of standardized VOI segmentation rules, time-activity curve modeling conventions, and auditable quality control and reporting procedures to improve reproducibility in both clinical trials and routine practice.

articles.title: Efficacy of [177Lu]Lu-PSMA-617 With and Without Androgen Receptor Pathway Inhibitors for mAPM-R Prostate Cancer: Secondary Analysis of VISION.
articles.abstract: The potential clinical benefit and impact on tolerability of combining androgen receptor pathway inhibitors (ARPIs) with [177Lu]Lu-PSMA-617 remain uncertain and were not evaluated in the primary analysis of VISION (NCT03511664). In this secondary analysis, we assessed efficacy and safety of [177Lu]Lu-PSMA-617 with and without concomitant ARPIs in previously treated patients (≥1 ARPI and 1 or 2 taxanes) with metastatic androgen pathway modulator-resistant prostate cancer (formerly metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer). Methods: Prostate-specific antigen (PSA) response, duration of PSA response, PSA progression-free survival (PSA-PFS), radiographic progression-free survival, overall survival (OS), and adverse events were explored in this post hoc analysis. For OS, a time-adjusted multivariate analysis was performed to control for biases. Results: Among patients randomized to [177Lu]Lu-PSMA-617, 289 versus 262 in the full analysis set and 283 versus 246 patients in the safety analysis set received treatment with and without concomitant ARPIs, respectively. Among patients treated with versus without ARPIs, 49.7% versus 42.2% had a PSA response (≥50% reduction in PSA level) (odds ratio, 1.41; 95% CI, 0.93-2.13; nominal 2-sided P = 0.103), with a median response duration of 9.4 mo versus 8.8 mo, respectively. The median PSA-PFS was 8.6 mo versus 7.3 mo (hazard ratio, 0.87; 95% CI, 0.70-1.09; P = 0.120 [nominal 1-sided stratified log-rank test]). A time-adjusted multivariate analysis showed a median OS of 16.6 versus 13.3 mo (hazard ratio, 0.79; 95% CI, 0.56-1.10; 2-sided P = 0.160). The frequency, nature, and severity of adverse events were similar between groups. Conclusion: The clinical benefits of [177Lu]Lu-PSMA-617 were similar with and without concomitant ARPIs. The addition of concomitant ARPIs to [177Lu]Lu-PSMA-617 provided a numerically higher PSA response and a numerically greater median PSA-PFS and median OS.

articles.title: Dynamic 18F-FDG Imaging of the Brain Using Total-Body PET in Patients with Genitourinary Cancer: A Pilot Study.
articles.abstract: Dynamic 18F-FDG PET enables brain kinetic quantification to study central nervous system involvement in cancer and other systemic diseases, but reliable blood input functions are difficult to obtain on conventional scanners. We used total-body PET to evaluate 18F-FDG kinetic modeling of the brain in healthy subjects and patients with genitourinary cancer (GUC). Methods: Ten patients with GUC and 12 healthy participants underwent a 1-h total-body 18F-FDG dynamic scan, and image-derived input functions were extracted from the aorta. Reversible and irreversible 2-tissue compartment (2Tr and 2Ti, respectively) models were assessed in the gray matter, thalamus, putamen, and brainstem using Akaike information criterion. Microparameters (K 1, k 2, k 3), net influx rate (K i), and practical model identifiability were assessed, and differences between patients with GUC and healthy participants were investigated. Results: The 2Tr model provided significantly better fits than the 2Ti model (P < 0.05). K i and SUV were significantly lower in patients with GUC across multiple brain regions. The 2Tr model revealed significant differences in K 1, k 2, and k 3 between the cohorts, independent of age, which were absent or attenuated when the 2Ti model was used. Identifiability analysis confirmed robust parameter estimation with reasonable bias and SD. Conclusion: Total-body dynamic PET enabled robust, noninvasive quantification of brain 18F-FDG kinetics using an image-derived input function. The 2Tr model provided superior time-activity curve fitting and identifiable parameters and revealed group differences in microparameters (K 1 and k 2) that were not detected with the 2Ti model. These findings suggest alterations in brain metabolism in patients with GUC, warranting further investigation.

articles.title: Unsupervised denoising of diffusion-weighted images with bias and variance corrected noise modeling.
articles.abstract: Diffusion magnetic resonance imaging (dMRI) plays a vital role in both clinical diagnostics and neuroscience research. However, its inherently low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), especially under high diffusion weighting, substantially degrades image quality and impairs downstream analysis. Recent self-supervised and unsupervised denoising approaches have shown promising potential without requiring clean reference images. However, most of these methods neglect the non-Gaussian statistical characteristics of noise in magnitude dMRI data, leading to biased estimation and suboptimal optimization under heteroscedastic noise. To address this limitation, we propose two Rician noise-aware loss functions that explicitly account for these characteristics. One loss function is derived from the first-order moment of the Rician distribution for signal bias correction, while the other leverages the second-order moment to perform bias correction through squared-signal statistics. Each loss further incorporates adaptive weighting based on the signal-dependent Rician noise variance to address heteroscedasticity. The proposed objectives are instantiated within an image-specific, unsupervised Deep Image Prior (DIP) framework without modifying the network architecture. Comparisons with state-of-the-art denoising methods on simulated and in vivo dMRI data demonstrate that the proposed approach yields higher image quality and more reliable diffusion metrics. These results highlight the importance of explicitly accounting for Rician noise-induced bias and heteroscedasticity in magnitude-domain dMRI denoising. Code is available at https://github.com/XieJine/Rician-Moment-DIP.

articles.title: Confocal microscopy segmentation via prototype-driven semi-supervised learning.
articles.abstract: The segmentation of anatomical structures like corneal nerves and Langerhans cells in in vivo corneal confocal microscopy is vital for diagnosing many ocular and systemic diseases. While deep learning offers a promising path to automation, its clinical translation is hampered by domain shift and a scarcity of labeled data across multi-center cohorts. To address these limitations, we propose Semi-NC, a semi-supervised framework that learns domain-invariant representations from both labeled and unlabeled data through a synergistic, four-step cycle: (1) extracting multi-scale prototype features, (2) refining them via feature amplification regularization, (3) constructing and updating category-specific prototype pools by aggregating features, and (4) aligning pixels to prototypes via contrastive learning to optimize the feature space for precise segmentation. Extensive evaluations on seven datasets (10,987 images across 22 diseases) show that Semi-NC sets a new state-of-the-art, outperforming fully-supervised baselines with minimal labels. The framework also demonstrates strong generalization under in-distribution and out-of-distribution tests, along with a robust self-evolution capability that allows it to extend its functionality using unseen data while preserving performance on learned tasks. Its broad clinical utility is further validated by superior performance on retinal optical coherence tomography angiography. To support reproducibility, we will open-source the code and the first multi-center, multi-disease dataset with high-quality annotations at https://github.com/iMED-Lab/Semi-NC.

Bridging Brain Connectome and Clinical Notes: A Novel Multimodal Framework for MCI Study.
articles.abstract: Integrating brain imaging data with clinical reports enables the effective use of complementary multimodal information, supporting more accurate and timely diagnosis in real-world clinical settings. This approach has gained growing attention in brain disorder research, yet significant limitations remain: how to encode brain structure and function to reflect meaningful neurological patterns, and how to effectively link objective imaging data with subjective text-based reports while establishing interpretable associations. In this work, we propose a novel multimodal framework that aligns brain connectomes with clinical reports in a shared cross-modal latent space at both subject and connectome levels. Our key innovation lies in treating brain subnetworks as tokens rather than raw image patches, enabling more efficient identification of system-level associations between neuroimaging findings and clinical observations. These cross-modal associations are further fused to enhance mild cognitive impairment (MCI) prediction and provide interpretable diagnostic insights. To our knowledge, this is the first attempt to integrate both structural and functional brain connectivity with non-imaging clinical information. Experimental validation on the ADNI dataset demonstrates performance competitive with recently reported methods. Notably, despite no explicit connectome-token-level supervision, the learned connectome-text associations recover multiple relationships independently reported in the neuroimaging and clinical literature, suggesting that the framework captures clinically coherent cross-modal associations. This pioneering work advances multimodal artificial intelligence (AI) for neurodegenerative disease diagnosis by bridging the gap between neuroimaging analysis and clinical text interpretation through innovative connectome tokenization and cross-modal alignment strategies.

articles.title: Ultrasound-guided microwave ablation for persistent or recurrent Graves' disease: long-term clinical and hemodynamic outcomes.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To evaluate 24-month clinical, biochemical, ultrasonographic, and safety outcomes after ultrasound-guided microwave ablation (MWA) for persistent or recurrent Graves' disease (GD) and to explore baseline factors associated with recurrence. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Twenty-four consecutive patients with persistent or recurrent GD despite at least 18 months of antithyroid drug (ATD) therapy were retrospectively analyzed. All patients underwent ultrasound-guided bilateral MWA. The primary outcome was complete remission at 24 months, defined as euthyroidism or hypothyroidism without ATDs. Secondary outcomes included thyroid function, thyroid-stimulating hormone receptor antibodies (TRAb), thyroid volume reduction, vascularity, and complications. Associations between baseline variables and recurrence were explored using univariable Cox regression. RESULTS: At 24 months, 20 patients (83.3%) achieved complete remission; 18 remained euthyroid and two developed subclinical hypothyroidism. Median thyroid volume reduction was 41.5%, and thyroid vascularity markedly improved. No transient or permanent recurrent laryngeal nerve palsy or other major complications occurred. Higher baseline free thyroxine (FT4) was associated with recurrence (HR: 1.07, 95% CI: 1.01-1.14, p = 0.028). A preliminary FT4 threshold of 39.11 pmol/L yielded an area under the curve of 0.71, but this estimate was based on four recurrence events and was not validated. CONCLUSIONS: Ultrasound-guided MWA was associated with favorable 24-month outcomes and an acceptable safety profile in selected patients with persistent or recurrent GD. The association between baseline FT4 and recurrence requires validation in larger controlled cohorts. KEY POINTS: Question Patients with persistent or recurrent Graves' disease need nonradiative, minimally invasive treatment options when antithyroid drugs fail and definitive therapies are declined. Findings Among 24 patients, microwave ablation achieved 83.3% complete remission at 24 months, reduced thyroid volume, improved vascularity, and caused no major complications. Clinical relevance Ultrasound-guided microwave ablation provided durable remission while preserving thyroid function in most selected patients who declined surgery or radioactive iodine.

Multicenter external validation of CT-based deep learning for proximal femoral fracture classification and quantitative fracture-line assessment.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To develop and externally validate a CT-based deep learning CAD system for proximal femoral fracture classification and fracture-line angle quantification and to preliminarily evaluate its clinical utility in a reader study. MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this multicenter retrospective study, coronal CT images from four institutions were used for training (259 patients, 19,844 annotated images) and internal validation (91 patients, 92 hips). External validation included 200 patients from independent institutions scanned with CT systems from two vendors. A ResNet-50-based convolutional neural network was used to perform fracture region segmentation, fracture classification, pelvic fracture detection, and fracture line angle estimation. The diagnostic performance and fracture-line angle agreement were evaluated using internal and external validation datasets. An exploratory reader study involving six readers was conducted to assess the effects of CAD assistance. RESULTS: Overall classification accuracy was 95.7% (κ = 0.944) internally and 91.5% (κ = 0.887) externally; F1-score ranges were 0.927-0.982 and 0.667-0.952, respectively. The fracture-line angle mean absolute errors were 4.54° and 6.26°, approaching the interobserver errors between orthopedic specialists (3.64° and 5.18°), with corresponding ICCs of 0.817 and 0.736, respectively. In the exploratory reader study, residents showed higher sensitivity with CAD assistance for non-displaced femoral neck fractures (0.78 vs. 0.47), with high specificity. CONCLUSION: This multicenter CT-based CAD system demonstrated accurate and generalizable fracture region segmentation, proximal femoral fracture classification, and objective fracture line angle quantification across independent datasets. The proposed approach has the potential to support diagnosis and preoperative assessment of proximal femoral fractures.

articles.title: Dual-domain fusion unfolding network for compressed sensing MRI.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Compressed sensing magnetic resonance imaging (CS-MRI) aims to recover high-quality MRI images from undersampled k-space data. Deep unfolding networks (DUNs) have shown strong potential in CS-MRI due to their interpretability and reconstruction capability. However, existing methods still face two limitations: insufficient modeling of the complex-valued structure of MRI data and inadequate utilization of complementary k-space and image-domain information. These limitations may cause detail loss or noise artifacts in reconstructed images. PURPOSE: This study aims to address these two challenges by developing a dual-domain unfolding framework that effectively integrates complementary information from the k-space and image domains for CS-MRI reconstruction. METHODS: This paper proposes a dual-domain fusion unfolding network (DDFU-Net) to address the aforementioned challenges by effectively integrating complementary information from the k-space and image domains. DDFU-Net introduces two core modules: the k-space reconstruction module (KRM) and the fusion attention module (FAM). The k-space reconstruction module processes complex-valued k-space data through real-imaginary decomposition and amplitude-phase representation modeling, with real-valued convolutional operations used for feature extraction. This design enables the network to exploit complementary information contained in the complex-valued k-space representation and improves detail recovery under high acceleration. The FAM promotes cross-domain interaction between the k-space and image-domain branches, enabling complementary feature fusion and improving detail restoration. A data consistency module is further incorporated to preserve the acquired k-space measurements during reconstruction. RESULTS: On the Brain and fastMRI datasets, DDFU-Net achieves competitive or superior reconstruction performance across the evaluated undersampling settings, with clear improvements in most comparisons. Ablation studies further validate the contribution of the major components. CONCLUSIONS: The proposed DDFU-Net achieves strong reconstruction performance under different undersampling settings, demonstrating the effectiveness of the coordinated dual-domain reconstruction framework.

articles.title: A dual-mechanism framework for imbalanced right ventricular ejection fraction estimation from 2D echocardiography.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Right ventricular ejection fraction (RVEF) is a clinically essential indicator of right ventricular systolic function and a well-established predictor of outcomes in cardiovascular disease. Reduced RVEF is strongly correlated with adverse clinical events such as heart failure progression, recurrent hospitalization, and increased mortality. Accurate and reliable estimation of RVEF is therefore crucial for risk assessment and guidance of treatment strategies. PURPOSE: Addressing the problem of imbalanced regression in RVEF estimation, we introduce a dual-mechanism framework that improves both robustness and generalization when learning from two-dimensional echocardiography (2DE) videos. METHODS: Our approach integrates Gaussian Kernel Constrained Mixup, which expands and smooths the training distribution via structured sample synthesis, and Feature Space Calibration, which imposes ordinal constraints on the latent representation using weighted contrastive learning. This combined strategy enhances both data efficiency and feature-label consistency across the entire value range. The well-trained model can be seamlessly integrated into clinical workflows to assist physicians in rapid patient screening. It enables efficient, high-throughput analysis of echocardiographic videos, providing reliable RVEF estimates that help identify high-risk patients at an early stage and support large-scale preliminary screening in resource-limited settings. RESULTS: On the RVENet dataset comprising 3583 echocardiographic videos, our method achieved state-of-the-art performance with a mean absolute error (MAE) of 4.03 ± 3.23 %  and an R 2  of 0.67. Evaluation on an independent external test cohort of 128 videos demonstrated generalization, with an MAE of 3.71 ± 2.54 %  . Stratified analysis confirmed consistent performance across diverse RVEF ranges, indicating robustness to imbalanced data distribution. CONCLUSIONS: The proposed framework effectively tackles data imbalance and regression bias in RVEF estimation through dual mechanisms that improve both sample diversity and feature discriminability. It exhibits good accuracy, generalizability, and balanced performance across the RVEF spectrum. The implementation of our approach is publicly available at https://github.com/Wnssl/DIRVEF.

articles.title: Magnetically enhanced peak-to-valley dose ratio for megavoltage photon minibeam radiotherapy.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Orthovoltage minibeam radiotherapy (MBRT) emerged as a promising strategy to reduce normal tissue toxicities while providing equivalent or superior tumor control compared to homogeneous target irradiation. These benefits arise from the sub-millimetric beam sizes and the highly heterogeneous dose distributions, typical for this technique. For MBRT operating at megavoltage (MV) photon energies, the lateral scattering of secondary electrons into the low dose regions poses a major limitation, compromising the therapeutic benefits observed in orthovoltage MBRT. Meanwhile, in presence of an inline magnetic field (IMF), parallel to the central axis of the incoming radiation beam, laterally scattered secondary electrons are forced onto helical trajectories around the magnetic field, thus being radially confined. PURPOSE: Investigate in-silico the effects of homogeneous IMFs with constant field strengths up to 15 T on MV-photon minibeams, with a view to confining secondary electrons radially and thus enhancing the peak-to-valley dose ratio (PVDR) compared to the case where no IMF is applied. METHODS: Monte Carlo simulations were performed using a simplified minibeam beam model. A digital water phantom (10 cm x 10 cm x 15 cm) was employed. The feasibility of four different minibeam geometries with respect to the PVDR enhancement at 14 cm depth in water with IMFs (0, 1.5 and 7 T) was investigated with mono-energetic (4, 10 and 18 MeV) photon minibeams. Out of the four geometries, the one for which the application of IMFs resulted in the most pronounced PVDR enhancement at 14 cm depth, was selected for the subsequent investigations. Using this geometry, the effects of IMFs up to 15 T on the PVDRs as a function of depth in water, were investigated for mono-energetic (2.5, 4, 6, 10, 15 and 18 MeV) photon minibeams and for a flattened (FF) Varian TrueBeam 6 MV photon energy spectrum. Finally, PVDR enhancement was investigated in a clinically motivated brain cancer case using the TrueBeam 6 MV FF photon energy spectrum with IMFs up to 15 T. RESULTS: Out of the four investigated geometries, the most pronounced PVDR enhancement at 14 cm depth in water was observed using the geometry with 1.0 mm beamlet width, 5.0 mm center-to-center spacing combined with 4 MeV beam energy and a 7 T IMF, increasing the PVDR from 2.6 ± 0.1 at 0 T to 16.0 ± 0.8 at 7 T. With this geometry, PVDRs enhancements occurred along the entire phantom for all investigated energies. At 14 cm depth in water the PVDRs were increased across the investigated beam energies by values between 10.4 ± 0.6 and 44.9 ± 3.7, when applying IMFs of 15 T compared to 0 T. The extent to which an IMF enhanced the PVDR was found to be dependent on the IMF strength, beam energy and depth in water. In the clinically motivated brain cancer case, a magnetic field of 6 T maintained a PVDR above 10 throughout the patient's head. CONCLUSION: The confinement of secondary electrons is possible with IMFs, therefore enhancing the PVDR for MV-photon minibeams.

articles.title: Development of a lung nodule volumetry tool for quality assurance assessment of low-dose lung cancer screening CT protocols.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Low-dose CT (LDCT) is the preferred modality for lung nodule detection and follow-up, yet standardized quality-control criteria are lacking. Volumetric accuracy is clinically important but strongly dependent on segmentation and reconstruction settings, particularly for small, low-contrast subsolid nodules, and frameworks for optimizing LDCT protocols based on volumetric performance remain limited. PURPOSE: To develop a lung nodule segmentation and volumetry tool that evaluates volumetric accuracy across CT reconstruction settings and to demonstrate how accuracy and repeatability metrics can support protocol comparison as a quality-assurance assessment. METHODS: A custom semi-automatic tool was developed in Python and evaluated using the QRM Thorax phantom on a GE Revolution Apex CT system. Fifteen artificial nodules were analyzed, combining five diameters (3-12 mm) and three attenuation levels (100, -630, -800 HU). Reconstruction parameters were systematically varied, including kernel (STANDARD, LUNG), slice thickness (0.625-2.5 mm), spacing (0.625, 1.25 mm), algorithm (DLIR-H and ASiR-V at 80%), and field of view (18, 36 cm). Performance was assessed using mean relative volume error (target within ± 20%), repeatability coefficient (RC), and size-specific RMSE; the best-performing configuration per nodule type served as reference. Reconstruction effects were evaluated using factorial ANOVA, Levene's test, Welch's t-test, and bootstrap analysis with false-discovery-rate correction. RESULTS: Overall mean relative volume errors ranged from -7.1% to 6.7% for solid nodules and -14.7% to 5.8% for type 1 subsolid nodules ≥ 5  mm; type 2 subsolid nodules showed larger deviations (-27.1% to -12.1%). Nodule size and reconstruction kernel were the dominant contributors to mean volume error, while slice thickness and spacing mainly influenced variability. Significant differences from the reference were found for four solid-nodule settings, none for type 1, and one for type 2 subsolid settings, with degradation occurring mainly at increased slice thickness or reduced field of view. The 3 mm subsolid nodules showed consistently high variability across all settings. CONCLUSIONS: The tool enabled quantitative comparison of CT reconstruction settings using volumetric accuracy and repeatability metrics. For clinically relevant sizes ( ≥ 5  mm), volumetric performance remained within the predefined technical-suitability range across most settings, supporting use of the tool for protocol evaluation and future dose-optimization studies.

articles.title: A meshfree method for robust evaluation of wall shear stress in patient-specific vascular geometries.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Wall shear stress (WSS) is an important hemodynamic marker of vascular disease, yet its accurate estimation in patient-specific geometries remains challenging. Because WSS is derived from the velocity gradient at the vessel wall, it is highly sensitive to how well the near-wall region is resolved. Finite-volume simulations on unstructured meshes can therefore yield inaccurate WSS values unless dedicated boundary-layer meshes are used, a difficulty that is amplified in complex, image-derived geometries where variations in vessel shape and curvature complicate gradient reconstruction at the wall. Methods that reconstruct wall velocity gradients accurately on irregular point distributions, without relying on specialized near-wall meshing, are therefore needed. PURPOSE: We present the meshfree Discretization-Corrected Particle Strength Exchange (DC PSE) methodology for accurate wall shear stress (WSS) computation in patient-specific vascular geometries represented by unstructured point clouds. METHODS: The proposed framework reconstructs spatial derivatives directly on irregular node distributions. The methodology is validated using fully developed Poiseuille flow, for which analytical solutions for both velocity and WSS are available. The proposed scheme is applied to transient blood flow simulations in patient-specific arterial geometries reconstructed from medical imaging. Mesh refinement convergence studies were performed to verify the accuracy and numerical robustness of the proposed approach. Velocity fields were computed by solving the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations using the OpenFOAM finite-volume solver, while WSS was evaluated from the reconstructed wall velocity gradients using the proposed DC PSE formulation. Numerical predictions were compared with WSS obtained directly from OpenFOAM. RESULTS: The proposed methodology accurately reproduced the analytical WSS distribution for the benchmark problem, achieving a normalized root mean square error (NRMSE) of 1.2 × 10 - 4    , compared with 1.2 × 10 - 2    obtained with OpenFOAM post-processing tools using a reference finite-volume solution. The reconstructed velocity derivatives remained stable on irregular point distributions. In patient-specific blood flow simulations, the proposed framework produced smooth and physically consistent WSS distributions throughout the cardiac cycle, accurately resolving regions of elevated and low shear associated with vessel curvature and bifurcations. CONCLUSIONS: The DC PSE framework provides an accurate, robust, and computationally efficient approach for WSS estimation in image-based cardiovascular Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) simulations. By improving the reconstruction of wall velocity gradients on complex geometries, the proposed methodology substantially enhances the accuracy of wall-derived hemodynamic metrics without requiring specialized boundary-layer meshes. The method offers a flexible post-processing framework that can be readily integrated into existing CFD pipelines and has significant potential for patient-specific cardiovascular modeling and computational medical physics applications.

articles.title: Revealing hidden vascular patterns: a modified CEUS LI-RADS framework for HCC using super-resolution ultrasound.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To investigate the incremental value of super-resolution ultrasound (SRUS) microvascular imaging in optimizing the contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS) liver imaging reporting and data system (LI-RADS) for the hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) diagnosis. METHODS: This prospective study enrolled high-risk patients for HCC from January 2024 to April 2025. Each patient underwent B-mode US, color Doppler flow imaging (CDFI), micro-flow imaging (MFI), conventional CEUS, and SRUS microvascular imaging examinations. Based on the two additional vascular features (capsular vessels and chaotic vessels) displayed by SRUS microvascular imaging, three novel criteria were developed for modified CEUS LI-RADS (LR). The LR-4 or LR-M lesions were reclassified to LR-5 using the following three criteria: (I) the presence of capsular vessels; (II) the presence of chaotic vessels; (III) the presence of capsular vessels or chaotic vessels. The diagnostic performance of modified CEUS LI-RADS using three HCC criteria was evaluated and compared with that of the original CEUS LI-RADS. The reference standard was pathologic confirmation or composite criteria. RESULTS: Overall, 593 patients with 593 lesions were enrolled. The visualization rate of the capsular and chaotic vessel features by SRUS is higher than that of CDFI, MFI, and the arterial phase of CEUS (all P < 0.05). The inter-observer agreement was substantial for capsular vessels (kappa = 0.742) and chaotic vessels (kappa = 0.631). Compared with the original CEUS LI-RADS, three novel criteria for modified CEUS LI-RADS demonstrated higher sensitivity, accuracy, and area under the curve (AUC) (all P < 0.05). Particularly, criterion III achieved the best sensitivity (89.80%), accuracy (89.38%), and AUC (0.891), without a significant decrease in specificity (88.48%). CONCLUSIONS: SRUS microvascular imaging is able to reveal hidden vascular patterns in refining CEUS LI-RADS for HCC diagnosis.

articles.title: Cross-View Constrained Encoder and Cross-Modal Semantic-Hierarchy Fusion Network for Congenital Heart Disease Identification.
articles.abstract: Congenital heart disease (CHD) is a common structural birth defect, and early screening is important for improving prognosis. Clinical cardiac ultrasound combines brightness-mode (B-mode) and color Doppler images from multiple standard views to assess cardiac morphology and hemodynamic abnormalities. Existing case-level models remain limited in modeling information exchange among standard views within each modality and cross-modal fusion between B-mode morphology and Doppler hemodynamics. The proposed Cross-View Constrained Encoder and Cross-Modal Semantic-Hierarchy Fusion Network (CVCE-CMSHFNet) addresses these limitations through two complementary components: a Multi-View Constrained Encoder (MVCE) and a Bidirectional Progressive Semantic-Hierarchy Fusion (BiPSHF) module. MVCE models relationships among the eight standard views within each modality. Sinkhorn-constrained transport and a parallel gated transformation update the view representations. Training-time Intra-Modal View Covariance Diversity Regularization (IVCDR) separately penalizes covariance similarity among B-mode view representations and among Doppler view representations. BiPSHF performs bidirectional cross-modal interaction at the view, view-group, and case levels. The view-group level organizes the eight standard views into four study-specific groups based on anatomical relationships and clinical assessment roles. CVCE-CMSHFNet aims to support clinical diagnosis by providing a case-level CHD probability for physician reference. Evaluation included 384 complete eight-view dual-modality cases from a 506-subject single-center echocardiography database. CVCE-CMSHFNet achieved 95.64% accuracy, 95.23% F1 score, 97.05% AUC, 94.44% sensitivity, and 96.67% specificity.

articles.title: Swin-DDM-Net: A Swin Transformer-Based Framework with Direction Difference Maps for Nuclear Instance Segmentation and Classification.
articles.abstract: Accurate nuclear instance segmentation and classification are fundamental prerequisites for quantitative digital pathology, but automated analysis remains difficult because nuclei vary substantially in shape, size, staining, density, and class-specific morphology. Swin-DDM-Net combines a hierarchical Swin Transformer encoder with three task-specific decoder branches for nuclear foreground prediction, horizontal-vertical distance regression, and pixel-level nuclear classification. The predicted distance maps are transformed into a Direction Difference Map (DDM), which captures local direction discontinuities at touching nuclear boundaries and refines marker-controlled watershed segmentation. Experiments on six public histopathology patch datasets, including CoNSeP, Kumar, CPM-15, CPM-17, TNBC, and CRCHisto, show competitive instance segmentation, patch-level cross-domain generalization, and nuclear classification performance relative to classical tools, convolutional baselines, HoVer-Net, CDNet, CellViT, and Mudslide under the evaluated settings. The results support the value of combining Transformer-based contextual representation with explicit instance geometry for cell-level computational pathology. The method should be interpreted as benchmark-level algorithmic evidence; statistical uncertainty analysis, dataset-license confirmation, public code and weight release, and external whole-slide-image (WSI) validation remain necessary before clinical deployment.

articles.title: PINet: A Pediatric Intussusception Network with Dual-Scale Guided Attention for Auxiliary Diagnosis Task Using Ultrasonography Images.
articles.abstract: Ultrasonography (USG) is the primary image modality for diagnosing pediatric intussusception, yet automated identification remains challenging due to severe bowel gas artifacts, acoustic reverberation, and edematous boundary blurring. Moreover, diagnostic uncertainty is exacerbated by the scarcity of large-scale clinical cohorts and ubiquitous acoustic speckle that frequently obscures critical pathognomonic landmarks. To address this gap, we propose Pediatric Intussusception Network (PINet) via a dual-scale guided attention to feature fusion trained on a large real-world pediatric intussusception dataset (RPID), which is used to predict anomalous classifications and improve lesion area learning. PINet integrates three complementary modules: (1) a position-attention module (PAM) to model concentric topological priors and suppress isolated gas artifacts; (2) a dual attention feature fusion (DAF) module combining strip pooling attention with dynamic alignment for multi-scale context aggregation; and (3) an informative context enhancement (ICE) module for low-contrast boundary refinement. It was trained on a largest reported dataset using 9871 USG images from 4026 patients. The result of PINet achieves state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance with 87.44% balanced accuracy and 98.09% area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). The clinical utility of the proposed PINet is demonstrated through robust performance across lesion sizes, accurate localization despite anatomical noise, and effective boundary delineation in low-contrast regions.

articles.title: Radiologist Workstation Configuration Preferences: Converging Evidence Toward Best Practices.
articles.abstract: Diagnostic radiologists spend much of their professional time interpreting imaging studies using a variety of workstation and monitor configurations. Despite well-established ergonomic principles, there are no widely accepted recommendations regarding monitor configuration, application placement, or peripheral device selection. This variability, particularly across academic medical centers with diverse workstation configurations, may contribute to musculoskeletal injury, workflow inefficiency, cognitive burden, and challenges integrating artificial intelligence (AI) applications. This study characterizes radiologist workstation configurations and determines whether similar usage patterns emerge across two independent national needs assessments. The findings from both assessments were compared. The first consisted of live audience polling during an RSNA 2025 educational session on radiologist ergonomics (n = 54). The second was an online survey distributed through professional LinkedIn and radiology social media communities (n = 49). Survey questions evaluated monitor number and orientation, workstation layout, application placement, ergonomic practices, sit-stand workstation use, and peripheral devices. Both assessments demonstrated similar workstation preferences. Most respondents in both the RSNA poll (n = 54) and online needs assessment (n = 49) used four-monitor equivalent configurations consisting of two portrait diagnostic monitors (often combined into one 30″ landscape) flanked by two supplemental monitors. Dictation was most commonly displayed on the left supplemental monitor, adjacent to the current examination (on the left diagnostic monitor). Respondents reported diverse placement of worklists, thumbnails, AI tools, peer review, electronic medical records, and advanced visualization applications. Sit-stand workstations were widely used, with most respondents standing 10-30% of the workday. Gaming mice with hyperscrolling functionality were the predominant pointing devices with very similar functions (window/level, measure, arrow, zoom/pan, and ROI). Two independent national needs assessments revealed consistent patterns in radiologist workstation configurations despite differences in survey methodology and participant populations. These findings suggest an emerging, flexible de facto standard that could guide ergonomic recommendations, workstation design and procurement, residency training, workflow optimization, and AI integration.

articles.title: Evaluation of a New CT Phantom Simulating the X-ray Attenuation of the Human Liver.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: To evaluate a new computed tomography (CT) liver phantom based on the International Commission on Radiation Units (ICRU) Report 46 composition of liver and adipose tissue (AT) and compare it with human studies calibrated against magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) proton density fat fraction (PDFF). MATERIALS AND METHODS: A liver phantom with seven inserts, ranging from 100% lean liver to 100% AT, was commissioned to reproduce the X-ray attenuation of the human liver by simulating the effective atomic number (Zeff) and electron density (ED) set out in ICRU Report 46. Five 120 kVp scans were acquired on each of nine CT scanners across five Chinese cities. Liver fat was measured using Mindways software calibrated to reproduce MRI PDFF measurements. Phantom data were compared with human CT and PDFF studies to assess reliability. RESULTS: Phantom insert measurements showed that 0% AT corresponded to 10.0% liver fat by Mindways, while 100% AT corresponded to 72.3%. Comparison of Mindways measurements with liver PDFF in 400 healthy volunteers showed agreement between the two fat scales. Dual-layer CT (DLCT) measurements of Zeff and ED matched the phantom manufacturer's specifications for the 0% AT insert (Zeff = 7.41; ED = 105.2%). However, linear regression of Zeff and ED against MRI PDFF in 99 healthy volunteers gave intercepts of Zeff = 7.18 and ED = 107.1% at 0% PDFF. CONCLUSION: DLCT measurements of Zeff and ED values in human livers were not consistent with similar scans of a phantom designed to simulate liver composition according to ICRU Report 46. However, measurements of the 100% AT insert were broadly consistent with the expected relationship between white AT and pure fat.

articles.title: Tumor-Associated Brain Metabolic Heterogeneity in Patients without Intracranial Lesions: A Multicancer 18F-FDG PET Study.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: Systemic malignancies may influence cerebral metabolism without direct intracranial involvement, but whether different tumor types are associated with distinct regional and network-level patterns remains uncertain. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study included 342 patients (219 men and 123 women) with colorectal, esophageal, gastric, or lung cancer, or lymphoma, who underwent 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography, together with 45 nontumor controls. Pons-normalized standardized uptake value ratios (SUVRs) from 25 brain regions were analyzed using multivariable linear regression and analysis of variance, with age, sex, tumor-related surgery, and treatment included in the models and false discovery rate correction applied. Univariable pairwise comparisons used Tukey adjustment. Principal component analysis and permutational multivariate analysis of variance assessed global patterns. Metabolic covariance networks were constructed using Pearson correlations, and topology and hub regions were evaluated. RESULTS: Analysis of variance identified regional differences among tumor groups, and several Tukey-adjusted pairwise comparisons were significant. Age and sex showed broader associations than surgery or treatment. Global metabolic patterns substantially overlapped across tumor types, without clear separation. Covariance networks differed in topology and hub distribution. In the full cancer cohort, lung cancer had sparse connectivity and the greatest number of hub regions, whereas esophageal cancer showed high local clustering without hubs. The no-intervention tumor groups and nontumor controls also showed different network topology and hub distributions. CONCLUSION: Brain metabolic covariance network analysis provides information on interregional metabolic organization alongside regional SUVR comparisons and global metabolic pattern analysis. The network findings require further validation.

articles.title: Quality and Determinants of Inpatient Imaging Requests: A Multicentre RI-RADS Study.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the quality and completeness of inpatient requests for general radiography, computed tomography, magnetic resonance imaging, and ultrasound using the Reason for Exam Imaging Reporting and Data System (RI-RADS), and to identify factors associated with request quality. METHODS: This retrospective multicentre study evaluated 1091 inpatient imaging requests across four hospitals. Requests were graded using RI-RADS. Associations between RI-RADS grade and hospital, requesting specialty, imaging modality, anatomical region, clinical indication, and patient characteristics were evaluated. Multivariable ordinal regression was used to identify independent determinants of poorer request quality, and interobserver agreement was assessed using Fleiss' kappa. RESULTS: Of 1091 requests, 141 (12.9%) were classified as RI-RADS grade A and grade D was the most frequent category (33.4%). An impression was documented in 62.1% of requests, whereas complete clinical information was present in only 19.4%. The multivariable model demonstrated explanatory performance of 46.3%. Hospital was the strongest determinant of RI-RADS grade; Orthopedic requests were associated with poorer documentation, whereas infection/inflammation and trauma, were associated with better request quality. Overall interobserver agreement was fair (Fleiss' κ = 0.231), with the highest component-level agreement observed for the diagnostic question. CONCLUSION: Inadequate clinical documentation was common in inpatient imaging requests, although its severity varied substantially across hospitals and clinical contexts. Request quality was primarily associated with institutional and clinical factors rather than imaging modality itself. The frequent absence of a diagnostic question and marked hospital-level variation identify potentially modifiable targets for structured referral systems, clinician education, and targeted quality-improvement initiatives.

articles.title: Reimagining the Future of Radiology Education in the Era of Artificial Intelligence.
articles.abstract: Rising clinical workloads and productivity pressures are reducing faculty time for teaching, mentorship, and educational innovation in radiology. This Perspective proposes that clinical efficiency gains from artificial intelligence (AI) be strategically reinvested in education through two complementary concepts. The educational dividend involves intentionally reinvesting a portion of time savings in teaching and mentorship, curricular innovation and scholarship, and faculty development. The educational multiplier describes how AI can extend the reach and impact across five domains: content creation, cognitive and perceptual learning, learning embedded in the clinical workflow, continuous assessment and feedback, and educational analytics. Neither the dividend nor the multiplier will be realized automatically; both require deliberate, sustained institutional commitment to strengthen radiology education.

articles.title: When Productivity No Longer Measures the Radiologist: The Cognitive Value Framework for Professional Value in AI-Enabled Radiology.
articles.abstract: Radiology has traditionally evaluated physician work using operational measures such as work relative value units, examination volume, and report turnaround time. These served as practical surrogates for physician contribution because operational workflow and diagnostic reasoning were historically performed together by the interpreting radiologist. Artificial intelligence (AI) is dissolving that coupling. AI increasingly performs routine operational tasks, yet radiologists must now evaluate AI-generated content, resolve discordance between AI output and their own interpretation, contextualize AI findings for patients and referring clinicians, and remain accountable for the result. By reducing operational effort while adding evaluative effort, AI may paradoxically increase rather than reduce higher-order cognitive work, and operational productivity and physician contribution diverge. This article introduces the Cognitive Value Framework, a conceptual theory of how radiologists-in academic and private practice alike-create Professional Value in AI-enabled practice. Its premise is that the primary professional product of radiology is clinically actionable diagnostic judgment rather than the report. Professional Value is generated through five interacting Domains of Professional Contribution: Operational, Cognitive, Clinical, Communication, and Accountability. Cognitive Friction is the central mechanism, distinguishing Productive Friction, which generates Professional Value, from Waste Friction, which does not. The Framework complements rather than replaces existing productivity metrics and offers a hypothesis-generating foundation for future investigation.

articles.title: Predictors Over Time of Occlusion Following Flow Diverter Treatment for Internal Carotid Artery Aneurysms: Insights from the INSPIRE-A Registry.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Flow diverters (FD) are integral to endovascular treatment-strategies for intracranial aneurysms. However, high-quality evidence on variables associated with procedural success after FD treatment is sparse and partially contradictory. PURPOSE: To analyze factors associated with complete occlusion (Raymond Roy Occlusion Classification [RROC] I) of internal carotid artery (ICA) aneurysms at various follow-up (FU) time points. METHODS: The INSPIRE-A registry is a prospective, single-arm study of aneurysms treated with FD. FU imaging was adjudicated by an independent imaging core laboratory. Patient characteristics, aneurysm details, and procedural variables were tested for association with RROC I at different FU (post-procedure, 6-,12-,24-month), using logistic regression analyses complemented by generalized estimating equations (GEE) across FU. RESULTS: Overall, 692 patients were included (median age, 55 years [IQR, 46-64]; 84.7% female). In multivariable analysis, adjunctive coiling was associated with RROC I post-procedure (aOR, 20.98; 95% CI, 6.27-70.22), older age at 6 and 12 months (aOR per year, 0.97; 95% CI, 0.96-0.99 and 0.95-1.00), male sex at 12 months (aOR, 0.32; 95% CI, 0.17-0.58), and current smoking at 12 months (aOR, 2.53; 95% CI, 1.30-4.96). GEE showed that the effect of adjunctive coiling decreased over time, whereas neck width was associated with lower odds of RROC I at 12 and 24 months only. CONCLUSION: This dataset, with independent imaging core lab adjudication, suggests that adjunctive coiling promoted early occlusion, whereas age, sex, smoking status, and neck width influence complete occlusion at later FU after FD treatment of ICA aneurysms.

articles.title: Baseline diffusion MRI markers of interstitial fluid dynamics are associated with subsequent amyloid conversion in cognitively normal individuals.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Emerging evidence suggests that early disruption of interstitial fluid (ISF) dynamics may precede amyloid-β (Aβ) deposition, and diffusion MRI-derived indices offer noninvasive markers of ISF properties. We investigated whether baseline ISF-sensitive diffusion MRI markers differ between Aβ-negative (-) cognitively normal (CN) individuals who subsequently convert to Aβ-positivity and those who remain Aβ (-), and whether these markers are associated with subsequent Aβ accumulation. METHODS: We included Aβ (-) CN participants from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative cohorts who had baseline MRI and longitudinal amyloid PET. Based on longitudinal amyloid PET standardized uptake value ratio (SUVR), participants were classified as 18 converters who exceeded the Aβ-positivity threshold at least once during follow-up and 16 non-converters who remained Aβ (-) throughout follow-up. Baseline diffusion MRI-derived ISF markers, cortical free water (FW), the diffusion tensor image analysis along the perivascular space (ALPS) index corrected for white-matter microstructural asymmetry (corrected ALPS index), and perivascular space volume fraction, were compared between groups, together with baseline Aβ, tau, and neurodegeneration biomarkers. Associations between baseline MRI measures and annualized change in amyloid PET SUVR were also assessed. RESULTS: Converters showed higher cortical FW and lower corrected ALPS index than non-converters, despite no baseline group differences in Aβ, tau, or neurodegeneration markers. Among converters, higher baseline FW was associated with a faster annualized increase in amyloid PET SUVR. CONCLUSIONS: Our findings indicate that baseline diffusion MRI markers of ISF dynamics are associated with subsequent Aβ-positivity conversion and Aβ accumulation in initially Aβ (-) CN individuals, suggesting that alterations in ISF dynamics may be detectable before overt Aβ deposition.

articles.title: Reference-Region Normalization Outperforms Data-Driven Approaches in [18F]FDG PET of Dementia with Lewy Bodies.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Data-driven intensity normalization has recently emerged as an alternative to proportional scaling (PS) and reference-region (RR) for brain [18F]FDG PET analysis. We investigate these methods in dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB; n=110, 72.1 ± 6.7 y/o) and healthy controls (HC; n=30, 67.6 ± 5.3 y/o) imaged with [18F]FDG PET/MR. METHODS: RR-based methods (pons, cerebellum, white matter), PS, iterative proportional scaling (iPS), histogram normalization (HN), iterative histogram normalization (iHN), and SUV conversion were evaluated through voxel-based comparisons (DLB vs HC). Scaling factors were extracted from the pons, cerebellum and white matter for RR, a gray-matter mask for PS, the modal voxel intensity in HN, and their subject-specific data-driven counterparts for iPS and iHN. For each scaling factor, we measured (i) their normative alignment between DLB and HC distributions; (ii) disease independence via correlation with a DLB meta-ROI; (iii) interindividual stability using coefficients of variation; and (iv) temporal stability based on longitudinal annual rates of change. These metrics were combined into a composite score to identify the optimal normalization approach. A simulation study on a Hoffman phantom was conducted to evaluate how each metric affects ground truth recovery. RESULTS: Widespread cortical hypometabolism was observed in DLB vs HC using RR and SUV normalization. In contrast, PS, iPS, HN, and iHN revealed cortical hypometabolism together with hypermetabolism in the sensorimotor cortex, basal ganglia, pons, and cerebellum (family-wise error-corrected p-value < 0.05). RR normalization yielded smaller DLB-HC differences in scaling factors, weaker correlations with the DLB meta-ROI, reduced coefficients of variation, and lower rates of change compared with PS, iPS, HN, and iHN. The white matter followed by the pons showed the highest composite scores. The simulation study showed that larger scaling-factor mean differences between patients and controls, and higher coefficients of variation, were associated with greater recovery error. DISCUSSION: This is the first systematic assessment of intensity normalization in the largest [18F]FDG PET DLB cohort to date. Our findings support RR-based normalization as the preferred standard in DLB, outperforming PS, HN and data-driven approaches.

articles.title: Towards the experimental assessment of exposure to extremely low frequency magnetic field.
articles.abstract: To perform an exploratory, body-resolved assessment of occupational exposure to motion-induced extremely low-frequency (ELF) magnetic fields in MRI environments. Although ELF exposure involves negligible energy absorption, physiological and sensory effects have been reported, and experimental evidence at frequencies below the power-frequency range remains limited.Approach: Twenty MRI operators were monitored during routine work shifts at 1.5 T and 3.0 T clinical scanners, using wearable gaussmeters at five body locations. Because these devices record only field magnitude, they give an approximate exposure estimate rather than the full Weighted Peak (WP) index defined in the ICNIRP guidelines. The dependence of the true WP on the characteristics of the motion was derived analytically. Numerical simulations of human gait in a virtual MRI environment were then used to show that the measurements capture only the translational contribution of body movement and neglect the rotational one.Main results: Even though the measured exposure is underestimated, the measurements frequently exceeded the ICNIRP-based Action Levels, particularly for the 3.0 T system.Significance: The results demonstrate that multipoint occupational exposure monitoring in MRI facilities is feasible, and they underscore the importance of accounting for realistic movement patterns in ELF exposure assessment. The proposed framework provides a basis for future studies aimed at refining dosimetric models and investigating exposure-response relationships.

articles.title: A depth-resolved single-flask 3D clonogenic platform for continuous LET-dependent radiobiological assessment in carbon-ion therapy.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Due to steep depth-dependent variations in radiation quality along carbon-ion beam paths, conventional point-wise clonogenic assays are labor-intensive and may inadequately capture biological responses across heterogeneous radiation fields. We developed a depth-resolved three-dimensional (3D) clonogenic assay platform that enables high-density spatial sampling, providing high-density radiobiological datasets for quantitative evaluation of biophysical models. APPROACH: A cell culture flask containing a uniform adherent cell layer was positioned at a defined tilt angle within a water phantom under carbon-ion beam irradiation. This geometry established a direct correspondence between water-equivalent depth and cell position, enabling depth-resolved mapping of physical dose, dose-mean lineal energy (yD), and clonogenic survival. Automated image processing and spatial reconstruction were used to generate survival profiles along the depth axis. MAIN RESULTS: The platform enabled millimeter-scale axial sampling with spatially registered spatially registered measurements of dose, yD, and clonogenic survival within a single-flask geometry. A549 and MDA-MB-231 cells were evaluated under monoenergetic carbon-ion beams and spread-out Bragg peak (SOBP) fields. Continuous depth-survival profiles, depth-dependent LQ parameters (α, β), and RBE10distributions were reconstructed across the particle range. Experimental results showed overall consistency with microdosimetric kinetic model (MKM) predictions while revealing localized deviations and cell-line-specific differences along the depth axis. SIGNIFICANCE: This study establishes a depth-resolved clonogenic assay platform for continuous characterization of LET-dependent radiobiological responses in carbon-ion beams. By enabling high-density spatial sampling, the platform provides a quantitative framework for evaluating particle-radiation-induced biological effects and generating depth-resolved datasets for validation and refinement of biophysical models.

articles.title: Multi-beam FLASH-RT preserves skin sparing and reveals novel tissue oxygen dynamics in a murine model.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: The goal of this project was to investigate whether the FLASH skin-sparing effect is preserved across multi-beam ultra-high-dose-rate (UHDR) deliveries and to characterize the accompanying in vivo tissue oxygen dynamics near a 5-second total treatment window previously shown to maintain sparing. APPROACH: Mice were irradiated at three dose levels (23.6, 25.2, and 25.9 Gy) across five experimental groups: single-beam UHDR, two-beam UHDR, sixbeam UHDR, twelve-beam UHDR, and conventional dose rate (CDR). To evaluate normal tissue toxicity, a skin damage cohort was monitored photographically for four weeks post-irradiation, with acute reactions evaluated by a trained observer. In a separate cohort, real-time tissue oxygenation (pO2) was tracked via a fiber-optic phosphorometer using the phosphorescent probe Oxyphor PtG4 to evaluate physiological kinetics independently of the longitudinal toxicity study. Main results. The FLASH skin-sparing effect was statistically indistinguishable for all experimentally tested UHDR configurations at the 23.6 Gy and 25.2 Gy dose levels. Mixed-effects regression analysis demonstrated that all four UHDR groups developed significantly lower skin toxicity scores compared to the CDR group (p < 0.05). At the highest dose level (25.9 Gy), no significant differences were observed among any radiation groups, which was attributed to a saturation effect of the visual skin score assay at severe damage thresholds. In vivo oximetry showed that tissue oxygen resupply accelerated during UHDR treatment, driven by localized concentration gradients and amplified post-RT by acute biological mechanisms. SIGNIFICANCE: This study represents a promising step toward UHDR multi-beam delivery, a prerequisite for clinical conformal treatment planning. Multiple UHDR beams delivered within five seconds provide a statistically indistinguishable degree of normal tissue sparing as a single UHDR beam. Furthermore, the observed tissue oxygen dynamics reveal an acute biological response potentially unique to UHDR delivery, shedding light on a novel physiological component of the FLASH mechanism.

articles.title: F²CW-MPI: deep Wiener reconstruction method with fusion prior of system matrix-signal feature correlation in magnetic particle imaging.
articles.abstract: Magnetic particle imaging (MPI) provides high sensitivity and spatial resolution for visualizing magnetic nanoparticles, but its system matrix (SM)-based reconstruction remains an ill-posed inverse problem that is highly sensitive to noise interference. Existing iterative and learning-based approaches typically embed denoising priors at the image-domain level within the reconstruction process, which limits robustness to noise variation, relies on manually tuned parameters, and underuses the physical information embedded in the SM.Approach. In this study, we propose F2CW-MPI, a non-iterative deep Wiener reconstruction framework. Unlike existing methods that embed denoising priors at the image-domain level, F2CW-MPI moves noise suppression earlier into the signal domain. An adaptive feature-refined Wiener denoiser estimates noise characteristics from latent signal features and dynamically adjusts denoising parameters accordingly, enabling signal-dependent noise suppression. Building on this design, a cross-attention-based fusion module then models the correlation between the denoised signal features and the SM within the same feature space, embedding the SM's physical prior into reconstruction. To reinforce this feature-level consistency, a joint loss function aligns the denoised signal features with ground truth features, together with image fidelity and concentration-distribution consistency terms. We evaluate F2CW-MPI on synthetic digital (training set: 6000 images; validation set: 2000 images; test set: 2000 images; with no overlap between sets) and vessel phantoms (training set: 80 subjects split into 28894 images; validation set: 10 subjects split into 2782 images; test set: 10 subjects split into 3078 images; with no overlap between sets), as well as real-world phantom data and in vivo data acquired on our homemade MPI scanner.Main results. Experiments show that F2CW-MPI outperforms iterative and existing learning-based methods in reconstruction accuracy and noise robustness, while preserving structural fidelity on real-world phantom and in vivo data.Significance. F2CW-MPI provides a robust and high-fidelity reconstruction strategy for MPI, showing potential for preclinical applications.&#xD.

articles.title: Optimizing radiobiological effects of119Sb targeted radionuclide therapy via DNA incorporation: a Monte Carlo simulation study.
articles.abstract: We investigate the hypothesis that the radiobiological effects of119Sb make it the most potent Auger electron-emitting radionuclide for targeted radionuclide therapy (TRT) of micrometastases. The objectives of this study were to evaluate radiobiological effects of119Sb decays in close proximity to DNA, to examine the sensitivity of the effects to the Auger electron spectrum model, and to compare these effects among contemporary Auger electron-emitters to determine if the effects of119Sb are the largest. Approach: TOPAS Monte Carlo was used to calculate dose-mean lineal energy, DNA strand breaks, and G-values within 10 nm of a simplified DNA double helix. Decay spectra were obtained from MIRD RADTABS07 and Geant4 Atomic Relaxation. The microdosimetric kinetic (MK) model was used to estimate the RBE relative to 200 kVp x-rays radiation with the assumption of equal, constant119Sb dose rate. Quantitative comparisons were made with103mRh,103Pd,111In,123I,125I,165Er, and197Hg. Main Results: Dose-mean lineal energy and DNA damage are maximized when119Sb is incorporated into DNA. In this highly idealized geometry, the dose-mean lineal energy is (189.37±0.06) keV/μm and the RBE is 3.2±0.6 ((σstat<0.01%)) which is indistinguishable from the competing radionuclides due to parameter uncertainties. Within 10 nm the RBE decreases by a factor of two. Abridging the Auger spectrum significantly underestimates these effects. DNA incorporation maximizes strand breaks at 2.2119±0.0016 (stat.) SSBs and 0.3207±0.0007 (stat.) DSBs per decay, which decrease by two orders of magnitude at 10 nm. Conversely, G-values of free radicals in the DNA volume increase with distance by an order of magnitude.119Sb yields relatively less DNA damage, and larger free radical yields than111In,123I and125I but smaller yields than103mRh,103Pd,165Er and197Hg. Significance: Localization of119Sb to the DNA double helix is critical to optimize radiobiological effects. Researchers developing119Sb TRT should therefore focus on solutions to achieve incorporation into DNA. In this highly-idealized geometry, RBE values are the same among the competitor radionuclides; however, more research is needed to account for exponential decay, clearance, and DNA repair before the RBE results can be interpreted categorically. Limitations in the strand break calculations point to the need to account for complex DNA damage and sublethal damage repair which may be more sensitive to the higher yield of119Sb Auger electrons.

articles.title: Denoising filters for fast Monte Carlo and genetic algorithm-based optimization.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the suitability of denoising filters for accelerating Monte Carlo (MC) dose calculation within genetic algorithm (GA) optimization frameworks for external beam radiation therapy treatment planning through preservation of optimization-relevant information in filtered low-statistic simulations. APPROACH: Gaussian smoothing, adaptive anisotropic diffusion (AAD), and wavelet threshold denoising (WTD) were applied to Geant4-generated three-dimensional MC dose distributions. Filter parameters were tuned across varying simulation conditions and evaluated using voxel-based dose agreement metrics. Filter performance within a GA framework was then assessed using multiple realistic objective functions, with optimization robustness quantified using Spearman rank correlation, winner identification, and winner consistency across repeated filtered MC dose calculations. MAIN RESULTS: MC particle statistics and voxel resolution had the strongest influence on optimal parameter selection for all three denoising filters, while beam energy, field size, and evaluation metric exhibited comparatively weaker effects. Filtering improved the ranking stability of candidate system configurations for low-statistic MC dose distributions, supporting faster evaluation within stochastic optimization algorithms. AAD filtering provided the highest ranking fidelity for objectives dependent on localized dose extrema, while WTD consistently identified the optimal configuration for dose-volume objectives across simulation statistics despite lower overall rank correlation. In contrast, Gaussian smoothing frequently degraded ranking fidelity for these objectives due to oversmoothing of important dose features. SIGNIFICANCE: Denoising filters can accelerate MC-driven optimization by enabling lower-statistic dose calculations while preserving optimization-relevant ranking information. Because optimal tuning depended primarily on particle statistics and voxel resolution rather than beam configuration, filter parameters can remain applicable across a wide range of candidate treatment setups. AAD and WTD showed the greatest promise for integration into MC-driven optimization workflows, with relative performance depending on the underlying MC noise level.

articles.title: Enhanced diffusion model with 3D structural and segmentation priors for lung cancer radiotherapy dose prediction.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Diffusion models show strong potential for high-fidelity radiotherapy dose prediction, but their performance depends heavily on the conditioning mechanism. This study introduces a novel conditioning strategy that improves volumetric consistency in slice-wise dose generation while reducing reliance on manually annotated organ-at-risk (OAR) masks. APPROACH: We propose a diffusion-based dose prediction framework conditioned on features from the full 3D computed tomography (CT) volume and a pre-trained medical image segmentation model. A 3D feature extractor encodes global anatomical information from the entire CT volume to preserve spatial coherence across 2D dose predictions. Rather than relying on manual OAR masks, the model uses anatomical representations from the pre-trained segmentation network, integrated via cross-attention to enable anatomy-aware dose prediction. MAIN RESULTS: The framework, Diff-Seg3D, was evaluated on three lung cancer radiotherapy datasets representing Volumetric Modulated Arc Therapy (VMAT), Fixed Gantry Intensity-Modulated Radiation Therapy (FGIMRT), and 3D Conformal Radiation Therapy (3DCRT) planning techniques. It achieved the numerically lowest mean absolute error (MAE) on all three datasets, with values of 3.16, 4.38, and 4.02 Gy, respectively, and the best dose-volume histogram (DVH) scores (2.64 and 3.82) on VMAT and FGIMRT, while remaining competitive on 3DCRT. Pre-trained 3D anatomical and segmentation encoders improved the baseline diffusion model, with segmentation features improving performance without requiring explicit OAR contours at inference. SIGNIFICANCE: This conditioning strategy improves volumetric consistency and anatomical awareness in diffusion-based dose prediction. The framework can serve as a tool for generating treatment-specific, anatomy-conditioned dose priors to guide radiotherapy planning.

articles.title: NOZOMI: a GPU-accelerated Monte-Carlo numerical approach for microstructure diffusion imaging.
articles.abstract: To develop an open-source computational framework for generating realistic white matter substrates and performing Monte-Carlo diffusion MRI simulations that use periodic boundary conditions to avoid artificial restrictions at substrate boundaries.Approach: A) A novel substrate generation algorithm was developed that ensures microstructure continuity across boundaries by adding reciprocal and replicated axons for boundary-crossing axons during substrate generation. B) A dedicated GPU-accelerated Monte-Carlo diffusion simulation engine was included, with multi-threaded CUDA implementation and simulation domain segmentation for computational efficiency. C) Validation and calibration experiments were done to verify geometric continuity across periodic boundaries, confirm simulation accuracy and precision against analytical solutions across diffusion times, compare against established simulators (Camino, Disimpy, MC/DC) under finite-pulse protocols, and guide simulation configuration. D) Diffusion time dependent axial and radial diffusivities across substrates with varying mean axon diameters and orientation dispersions were evaluated to demonstrate the utility of the framework.Main results: The framework successfully constructed complex biomimetic white matter substrates achieving high packing densities with controlled diameter distributions, orientation dispersions, beading morphology, and myelination. Monte-Carlo simulations reveal that, in both intra- and extra-axonal spaces, axon diameter primarily influences time-dependent radial diffusion, while fiber orientation dispersion primarily impacts axial diffusion.Significance: The developed framework is the first 3D white matter simulation framework to implement periodic boundary conditions for Monte-Carlo simulations without geometric discontinuity, providing approximately four times faster substrate generation than comparable tools, while facilitating controlled investigations of compartment-specific diffusion time dependence of microstructure-diffusion relationships.
